lines.say: This is Claim Check. It answers one question for Indian families: will my health insurer pay at this hospital?

Insurers keep lists of hospitals where they won't pay claims. Since 2024, Cashless Everywhere lets you go cashless outside your insurer's network, but not at a hospital it has blacklisted. And those lists are PDFs, replaced without notice or history.
lines.caption: Cashless Everywhere works outside your insurer's network, but not at hospitals it has blacklisted. Those lists are PDFs, replaced without notice.

lines.say: The card on the home page is a real record, read live from Arkiv. HDFC ERGO dropped Rama Hospital in Sonipat in March 2026. Tata AIG still excludes it.
lines.caption: A real record, read live from Arkiv: HDFC ERGO dropped Rama Hospital in March 2026; Tata AIG still excludes it.

lines.say: Every row names its source: the insurer's PDF, the row and page it came from, and the read-only Arkiv record behind it.
lines.caption: Each row names its source: the PDF version, row and page, and the read-only Arkiv record.

lines.say: Between 2024 and 2026, eighteen hundred and fifteen hospitals left HDFC ERGO's list, and eight hundred and seventy-eight joined. Nobody announced it.
lines.caption: 2024 to 2026: 1,815 hospitals left HDFC ERGO's list and 878 joined. Nobody announced it.

lines.say: Search any hospital or PIN code. Gaurav Hospital is the reverse case: HDFC ERGO still excludes it, while Tata AIG removed it in July 2025.
lines.caption: The reverse case: HDFC ERGO still excludes Gaurav Hospital; Tata AIG removed it in July 2025.

lines.say: Every version is compared with the one before it. HDFC ERGO's March 2026 list added eight hundred and seventy-eight hospitals, and dropped eighteen hundred and fifteen.
lines.caption: Every version is compared with the one before it. HDFC ERGO, March 2026: +878, −1,815.

lines.say: It's broken down by state, and you can filter by hospital, city, or PIN.
lines.caption: Broken down by state, and filterable by hospital, city or PIN.

lines.say: Each list version is its own Arkiv entity, carrying the SHA-256 hash of the PDF. HDFC's link labelled twelfth of February 2025 actually serves a file created in March 2026. We record what the file is, not what it's called.
lines.caption: Each version is an Arkiv entity with the PDF's SHA-256. HDFC's link labelled 12-02-2025 serves a file made in March 2026.

lines.say: Anyone can check our work. Replay reads every event from Arkiv at a single block, and compares each version's count with its source.
lines.caption: Replay: read every event from Arkiv at one block and check each version's declared count.

lines.say: All thirteen versions, seven thousand two hundred and sixty-eight events. Consistent.
lines.caption: All 13 versions, 7,268 events: consistent.

lines.say: Freshness is a fourteen-day lease. We re-download each PDF, and only if the hash matches do we extend it, with extendEntity. If it lapses, the page says stale, never safe.
lines.caption: Freshness is a 14-day lease, renewed with extendEntity only if the PDF's hash still matches. Lapse means 'stale'.

lines.say: Freshness is a fourteen-day lease. Right now, we re-download each insurer's PDF, and since the hash matches, extendEntity renews it.
lines.caption: Freshness is a 14-day lease. We re-download each PDF; if the hash matches, extendEntity renews it…

lines.say: And every open page hears about it live, over a WebSocket subscription. If a lease ever lapses, the page says stale, never safe.
lines.caption: …and every open page learns about it live, over a WebSocket. Lapse means 'stale', never 'safe'.

lines.say: There's no backend. The same answer comes from a zero-dependency command line tool, straight from Arkiv, trusting only our publisher's address.
lines.caption: No backend: the same answer from a zero-dependency CLI, straight from Arkiv, trusting only our publisher's $creator.

lines.say: Claim Check. Two insurers, thirteen list versions, and every change, on the record, on Arkiv.
